issue.title: sase artifact read never commits its link rows, so ~45% of recorded read edges are lost
issue.description:
`sase artifact read` records a `read` link row that is never committed, so the row is
destroyed with the ephemeral workspace and vanishes from the aggregate on the next
rebuild.

Measured on 2026-08-24 at `cbea4f23b`: the project read log
(`~/.sase/projects/gh_sase-org__sase/artifact_reads.jsonl`) holds 145 events with
`recorded_link: true`, covering 140 distinct `(agent, ref)` pairs. The live link graph
holds **78** read rows. 63 recorded pairs (45%) have no durable row; 56 of them are
`plan:` targets.

Root cause: `handle_link_add` (`src/sase/artifact_cli/link_ops.py:158`) calls
`store.upsert_row(...)` **and then** `_persist_link_mutation(...)` ->
`persist_artifact_link_graph_mutation`, which commits each sidecar it changed.
`_record_read_link` (`src/sase/artifact_cli/read.py:243`) calls `store.upsert_row(...)`
and stops. `persist_artifact_link_graph_mutation` has exactly two call sites, both in
`link_ops.py`.

The row therefore lands only in the ephemeral workspace's clone of the sidecar working
tree. `upsert_row` finishes by calling `rebuild_aggregate()`, documented as "rebuild
``artifact-links.json`` from sidecar JSON plus bead events" - a full rescan of the
current working tree. The next agent, in a different workspace whose sidecar clone was
just fast-forwarded to origin, rebuilds from a clean checkout and the uncommitted rows
disappear from the machine-local aggregate too. The rows that survived are the ones
whose workspace happened to run a `link add` or a projection commit afterward.

This is hazard #1 of the original design (`research:202608/artifact_link_graph/artifact_link_graph.md`,
"index silently uncommitted") re-emerging on the write path that generates 57% of all
link volume.

The naive fix is to call `persist_artifact_link_graph_mutation` from `_record_read_link`.
That is probably correct but deserves one design decision first: reads run ~37/day and
would each produce a sidecar commit and push, so consider batching the persist at turn
end (the finalizer already commits sidecars) rather than per read.

Add a doctor counter comparing `recorded_link: true` events against durable rows so the
leak cannot silently return.

task_type_fields.impact: Silently destroys 45% of the highest-volume automatic link writer's output, so the artifact link graph under-reports what agents actually read; also makes any future derived-link work leak the same way.
task_type_fields.repro:
Measured at `cbea4f23b`, 2026-08-24:

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
P="~/.sase/projects/gh_sase-org__sase/artifact_reads.jsonl"
ev=[json.loads(l) for l in open(__import__("os").path.expanduser(P)) if l.strip()]
rec=[e for e in ev if e.get("recorded_link")]
pairs={(e["agent_name"], e["ref"]) for e in rec}
print("recorded events:", len(rec), "distinct pairs:", len(pairs))
PY
sase artifact link list -j -l 0 | python3 -c "import json,sys; r=json.load(sys.stdin); print('read rows:', sum(1 for x in r if x['relation']=='read'))"
```

Output: 145 recorded events / 140 distinct `(agent, ref)` pairs against 78 durable read
rows. 63 pairs (45%) have no row.

Then confirm the write path never persists:

```bash
grep -rn "persist_artifact_link_graph_mutation" src/sase | grep -v "def persist"
# only src/sase/artifact_cli/link_ops.py:154,158 - never read.py
```

payload.description: both are inflow defects in the same artifact-link write path found in one measurement pass; sase-t1's fix touches the same upsert_row callers
